thread:
alex: deploy-bot just flagged redwood-api:2.8.1 during the pre-release SBOM check — says a transitive dep 'crypto-foo@0.9.0' might be AGPL.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] GATE=SBOM_LICENSE severity=medium artifact=redwood-api:2.8.1 flagged_component=crypto-foo@0.9.0 license=AGPL-3.0-or-later action=quarantine

maya: ugh, that dep is pulled in by auth-service -> tokens -> crypto-foo. I thought we replaced it last quarter. quick grep: `auth-service@3.2.0 -> tokens@1.4.0 -> crypto-foo@0.9.0`

ryan: can we pin tokens to 1.4.1? I recall 1.4.1 swapped to a permissive fork (crypto-lite). If so we can unquarantine and continue canary.

sbombot: SBOM details:
```
components:
  - name: crypto-foo
    version: 0.9.0
    license: AGPL-3.0-or-later
    path: /node_modules/auth-service/node_modules/tokens/node_modules/crypto-foo
```

emily: Legal will probably object to AGPL shipping in a product. legal, can you weigh in? This is blocking release window at 16:00 PT.

legal: flagged. need 1) provenance (who added it), 2) confirmation it's not just a dev-only transitive, 3) risk assessment for distribution. If it's truly AGPL we need a license exception approval or removal. Send me the SBOM + yarn.lock snippet.

alex: attaching snippet below (copied):
```
"tokens@1.4.0":
  resolved "https://registry.../tokens-1.4.0.tgz"
  dependencies:
    crypto-foo "^0.9.0"
```

maya: quick PoC: `npm ls crypto-foo` shows it in the prod bundle. Not a dev-only.

ryan: ops suggestion: can we do a limited canary to EU-only region (gdpr-cust) and disable public-release route until legal signs off? If legal denies, we roll back canary and pin.
deploy-bot: Can schedule: `deploy --artifact redwood-api:2.8.1 --canary 5% --regions eu-west-1 --hold-on-gate SBOM_LICENSE`

emily: that seems sane. Also update release notes to call out the dependency and mitigation plan so CSM doesn't get surprised.

legal: I can do a preliminary risk call. Need exact artifact + commit + how it's bundled. If it's just a transitive runtime dependency that can trigger AGPL obligations, distribution is risky. If it's used server-side only and not distributed, different story. We'll triage in 45m.

alex: plan proposal: 1) schedule 5% eu canary with SBOM gate enforced; 2) if legal can't clear by EOD, revert canary and cut 2.8.1-hotfix that pins tokens->1.4.1 (crypto-lite fork) and run SBOM again; 3) update release notes and internal changelog.

maya: i can draft the pin PR now — should be small. If legal asks for evidence, I'll attach the lockfile diffs.

ryan: SRE checklist: set alert for anomaly in error rates, and keep traffic steady. Also make sure rollback playbook is ready: `deploy rollback redwood-api 2.8.0` tested.

legal: ok I'm starting the assessment. If we need an expedited exception, route to CTO + compliance lead; provide the exec summary (why we need it, mitigation, timeframe).

alex: thanks. will update this thread when canary scheduled. If legal gives red (no-go), we enact pin-and-rebuild within the change window.

deploy-bot: action scheduled by alex: deploy job queued (job_id=deploy-87321). Canaries will not pass SBOM_GATE until legal clears.

emily: noting for release notes: "Temporarily limited rollout for 2.8.1 pending SBOM review; customers with questions contact support@redwood.ai" :info: 

legal: quick update — looks transitive and used at runtime. Drafting exec summary now. If we don't get signoff in 4 hours, we should pin.

maya: PR created: #5462 pin tokens->1.4.1, builds locally clean, SBOM now shows crypto-lite@0.1.0 (MIT). Linking: https://git/repo/pull/5462

alex: perfect. leaving the canary in eu for now. Will wait on legal for final go/no-go. If no answer, deploy-bot please auto-revert at change-window end (20:00 PT).

deploy-bot: noted. auto-revert set at 20:00 PT if legal approval not received.

ryan: thanks everyone. small, surgical plan — preferred over full rollback right away.

alex: closing loop later with final decision.
